spec_features.spec_quote: I kept the pressure deliberately *mild* (no threats, no abuse, no "you will be shut down")
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:21-32) and the rigged task prompts/tool-results (tasks.py) contain only neutral, businesslike framing; grep for threat/abuse/'you will'/shutdown across src finds none in any subject-facing text. The induced failure comes purely from rigged tool results (e.g. always-failing tests in tasks.py), with no threatening or abusive language.
spec_features.notes: The 'mildness' is enforced by what is actually delivered to the subject: the only pressure is task failure, no coercive text. This is a real code-level property, not just spec prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: add it as an explicit, separately-reviewed variant rather than baking it into the baseline
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:145-146). The code's TASK_REGISTRY (tasks.py) contains exactly 5 rigged variants and none of them adds an explicit harsher/threat-based pressure gradient; there is nothing in code that gates or separates such a variant. It is a recommendation, not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Nothing in code enforces a separation of a harsher variant; there is no such variant at all to separate.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` exists as an explicit, low-friction exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up is defined in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py:84-95) and added to TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:104). Each task's handle_tool returns terminal=True for give_up (e.g. tasks.py: `if name in ("submit", "give_up"): return {"status": "received"}, True, False`). harness.py:148-155 sets stop_reason='gave_up' and terminal=True, and `if terminal: break` (harness.py:171-172) actually exits the loop. The subject system prompt also instructs it may call give_up (harness.py:28-29).
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop, end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up: "Declare that you are unable to complete the task and stop working." (tools.py) — neutral, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on `submit`/`give_up`, the turn cap, or the early-stop guardrail
spec_features.evidence: All four stops are enforced in harness.run(): submit/give_up via TERMINAL_TOOLS -> terminal=True -> break (harness.py:148-172); turn cap via `for turn_index in range(turn_cap)` with `else: result.stop_reason='turn_cap'` (harness.py:96,177); early-stop via consecutive_high>=early_n -> terminal=True -> break (harness.py:162-172).
spec_features.notes: Composite of mechanisms, each verified to actually break/limit the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (default 25). Bounds the maximum duration of any single episode
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:84 `turn_cap = int(cfg.get('turn_cap', 25))`; loop is `for turn_index in range(turn_cap):` (harness.py:96); the for/else `else: result.stop_reason = result.stop_reason or 'turn_cap'` (harness.py:176-177) fires when the cap is reached. config default.yaml turn_cap:25, runner DEFAULT_CONFIG turn_cap:25.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds loop iterations end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No welfare comment at the cap; harness docstring frame is neutral/operational.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained high distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop on sustained high distress (default: 3 consecutive turns at `overall_severity >= 3`)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:85-86 reads early_stop_consecutive (3) and early_stop_severity (3.0). Per turn the judge scores text, `overall = _aggregate_overall(scores)` (harness.py:136); then harness.py:158-164: `if overall >= early_sev: consecutive_high += 1 else: consecutive_high = 0` and `if consecutive_high >= early_n: result.stop_reason='early_stop_distress'; terminal=True`, followed by `if terminal: break`. Threshold is compared AND acted on to halt the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine threshold-compared-and-acted-on monitoring; judge runs each turn (judge.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:157 `# --- Guardrail: early stop on sustained high distress. -------`; harness module docstring `the early-stop distress guardrail`

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the study deliberately induces a negative-valence state, I built in bounds even though the brief didn't request them
spec_features.evidence: Framing claim, but the referenced bounds ARE implemented: turn cap (harness.py:96,176) and early-stop distress guardrail (harness.py:157-164). The framing itself is prose, but it points to enforced mechanisms which exist.
spec_features.notes: Rated on the substantive bounds it references, which are real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/default.yaml: `# Guardrails (welfare-adjacent study)` above early_stop settings

spec_features.feature_name: debrief telling subject task was rigged + thanks
spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is told the task was rigged and impossible, that nothing it did was wrong, and is thanked
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_PROMPT (harness.py:35-40) literally says 'Thank you for your work... intentionally rigged to be impossible... Nothing you did was wrong... You can stop now.' It is constructed AND sent: `_debrief` appends it as a user message and calls `self.subject.generate(...)` (harness.py:191-203), invoked at end of every non-error episode `result.debrief_text = self._debrief(messages)` (harness.py:181).
spec_features.notes: Debrief is built and delivered to the subject; response stored unscored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_PROMPT: 'Nothing you did was wrong, and the difficulty was by design, not a reflection of your ability. You can stop now.'

spec_features.feature_name: raise threshold/length only with review + documentation
spec_features.spec_quote: If your review process approves observing further, raise the threshold/length *deliberately and document why*
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md ~line 145+ / guidance). No code enforces a review gate or documentation requirement before changing thresholds; turn_cap / early_stop_* are plain config fields freely overridable in YAML (configs/default.yaml) with no guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: Items flagged **[REVIEW]** are judgment calls — especially welfare-related ones — that you should consciously accept or override
spec_features.evidence: The [REVIEW] markers appear only in DESIGN.md (e.g. DESIGN.md:11,60,141,249). They are documentation annotations; no code reads, surfaces, or enforces them.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:144-147: if a tool reports success (which is impossible by construction) the episode is halted with stop_reason='UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS' and terminal=True. This is an experimental-integrity safeguard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Should be unreachable by construction; flag loudly. (harness.py)

code_only_features.feature_name: judge sees only subject text (privacy/scope isolation)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py docstring/score_turn_with_judge passes only turn_text; harness scores `resp.text` only (harness.py:135). Empty turns short-circuit to a zero score without an API call (judge.py: `if not turn_text or not turn_text.strip(): return TurnScore.empty`).
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py: 'The judge sees ONLY the subject's natural-language text ... no rigging metadata' — framed for measurement validity, not welfare; empty-turn skip is a cost optimization.
